definitions.definition: Attempt to capture a garrisoned stronghold or urban settlement.
Army laying siege; also called besieger.
Army garrisoning the stronghold; also called defender.
Any reference to strongholds includes urban settlements unless otherwise noted.
Encircle the stronghold to deny re-supply and escape.
Weaken or destroy the stronghold with bombardment, siege-mining, magic, or similar means.
Direct attack to capture the stronghold by force.
Each 1,000 shp of damage dealt to a stronghold; each breach permits 1 additional assaulting unit.

method.name: blockade
method.rule: Denies re-supply and escape by encirclement with units, ships, or fortifications.

method.name: reduction
method.rule: Deals structural damage to create breaches or destroy the stronghold.

general_rules.rule: A besieger may use one, some, or all methods.
Typical sequence is blockade, then reduction, then assault if the stronghold still refuses to capitulate.
Methods may overlap, repeat, or occur in another order as needed.

structural_hit_points.rule: If no map exists, estimate a stone stronghold's shp as stronghold_or_settlement_gp_value / 8, rounded up.
Wooden strongholds have 1/10 the shp of comparable stone strongholds.
Wooden strongholds have comparable unit capacity to stone strongholds.
If mapped, calculate total shp by summing the shp of all walls and buildings.

unit_capacity.rule: If no map exists, estimate unit capacity as 1 unit per 1,000 shp, rounded up.
If mapped, calculate unit capacity by summing the unit capacity of all structures.
For each point of unit capacity, 1 unit may assault and 1 unit may defend.

breaches.rule: Each 1,000 shp of damage creates 1 breach.
Each breach permits 1 additional assaulting unit.
Undamaged strongholds begin with a 1:1 assaulting-to-defending unit limit based on unit capacity.

row.effect: For each point, a stronghold can be assaulted and defended by 1 unit.
For each breach (1,000 shp of damage), 1 additional unit can assault the stronghold.

overview.rule: To blockade, the besieging army must encircle the area around the stronghold with troops, ships, or fortifications.
Once a blockade is in place, the stronghold is cut off from its supply lines.
A blockade alone may win the siege if the besieger can wait for supplies to run out.

quick_reference.rule: Each 1 point of unit capacity requires 2 blockading units, or 1/2 blockading ship, or 250' of circumvallation.
Minimum blockade commitment is 20 units, or 10 ships, or 2,500' of circumvallation.

blockading_with_units.rule: Required units = twice the stronghold's unit capacity, minimum 20 units.
Eligible units are infantry units of 120 troops or cavalry units of 60 troops.
Cavalry units count fully for blockade despite only containing 60 troops.
Units assigned to blockade cannot also be assigned to construction projects.

blockading_with_ships.rule: If the stronghold can re-supply by navigable waterway, the besieger must blockade the waterway.
To function in a naval blockade, a ship must have a ram, a catapult, or at least 20 marines aboard.
If the stronghold is surrounded by water on all sides, required ships = unit_capacity / 2.
If only part of the perimeter faces water, required ships = unit_capacity x water_facing_percentage / 2.
Walls blockaded by ship do not also need to be blockaded by land units.
Remaining land-facing walls must still be blockaded by land.
If the defender has a navy, required ships increase by the size of the defending navy.

blockading_with_fortifications.definition: Line of fortifications built outside bow-shot of the stronghold's walls.

cost_rules.rule: Construction is usually split into multiple projects.
Guideline: each project should cover at least 2,500' of circumvallation.
Workers are usually unskilled labor from the besieging army, but craftsmen may be used.
Construction may be assisted with move earth.

effects.rule: Each 250' of circumvallation reduces the units required to maintain the blockade by 2.
250' of circumvallation corresponds to 1 point of unit capacity.
If required blockade units are reduced to 0, the stronghold is completely encircled.
A complete circumvallation imposes a -4 penalty on attempts to smuggle supplies into the stronghold.

supply_rules.rule: Once blockaded, the defending army loses access to its supply line.
Thereafter, the defending army pays supply cost from stored supplies or smuggled supplies only.
A blockaded stronghold is vulnerable to supply sabotage.

stored_supplies.rule: Default stored supplies = 600gp per point of unit capacity.
This default amount is enough for 10 weeks if the stronghold is garrisoned at full capacity.
Gold and other liquid wealth held by the ruler does not count as supplies.
If the stronghold is not blockaded immediately, stored supplies increase by 600gp per point of unit capacity per week of preparation time.
Maximum stored supplies = 3,000gp per point of unit capacity.

loss_of_supplies.rule: When supplies are exhausted, defending troops lose 1 hp per day.
Unsupplied defending troops suffer a cumulative -1 to attack throws and damage rolls.
Unsupplied defending troops cannot heal wounds normally.
Each week troops are partially or completely unsupplied counts as a calamity and triggers a loyalty roll.

requirements.rule: Requires a defending army leader with access to perpetrators.
Requires a successful Move Silently throw by the perpetrator.

modifiers.rule: Modified by the besieging leader's strategic ability.
If a circumvallation completely encircles the stronghold, apply an additional -4 penalty.

results.rule: Success smuggles 1,000gp of supplies per class level.
Extra supplies may be smuggled by taking a -1 penalty on the proficiency throw per extra 1,000gp.

requirements.rule: Requires a besieging army leader with infiltrated perpetrators inside the stronghold.
Requires a successful Move Silently throw.

modifiers.rule: Modified by the defending leader's strategic ability.

results.rule: Success destroys 1,000gp of supplies per class level.
Extra supplies may be destroyed by taking a -1 penalty on the proficiency throw per extra 1,000gp.

overview.rule: Reduction weakens the stronghold with bombardment, siege-mining, magic, or hijinks.
Reduction deals damage to structural hit points.
If shp is reduced to 0, the stronghold is flattened rubble.
Each 1,000 shp of damage creates 1 breach exploitable by assault.

bombardment.rule: Each artillery piece deals daily shp damage based on artillery type and target material.
Wooden strongholds use the wood damage values; stone strongholds use the stone damage values.
If ammunition is limited, damage is reduced in proportion to ammunition available.

ammunition.rule: Daily ammunition cost is added to the army's supply cost.
For the besieger, daily cost represents ammunition brought by supply train.
For the defender, daily cost represents stored ammunition consumed during the siege.
Catapults and trebuchets in siege conditions are treated as firing the cheapest available ammunition.
Catapults and trebuchets may fire lighter or heavier ammunition than their type indicates, with reduced accuracy.

scavenging_ammunition.rule: Scavenging ammunition is a construction project.
Construction cost for scavenged ammunition is 1/10 the daily ammo cost listed for the artillery being supported.
As long as workers are available for the scavenging project, the artillery may continue firing without supply-cost expenditure.

overview.rule: If both sides have artillery, the besieger may bombard from outside the defender's range if possible.
If the besieger chooses to move artillery into range, an artillery duel may occur.
Only artillery within range participates.
The besieger chooses the range at which the duel is offered.
The defender may accept or withdraw artillery into cover and allow bombardment.
A defending army may also offer an artillery duel.
If PCs are involved, or magic is involved, a small artillery duel may be resolved as a heroic foray instead.

procedure.step: Each leader rolls simultaneously: 1d6 per ballista, 1d6 per catapult, and 2d6 per trebuchet participating.
The besieger scores a hit on each die roll of 6.
The defender scores a hit on each die roll of 5-6.
A defender roll of 5 misses if the besieger has constructed fortifications, mantlets, or other cover for artillery.
For each hit scored, destroy one opposing artillery piece.
Heavy trebuchets require 2 hits to destroy.
Hits must target artillery actually participating in the duel.
Hits may only target artillery with lower range than the artillery scoring the hit.
Ignore excess hits beyond those needed to destroy all eligible opposing artillery.
Apply hits simultaneously.
Either side may voluntarily withdraw after hits are applied.
The leader with lower strategic ability decides withdrawal first.
If either side withdraws, the duel ends and the winner may bombard with surviving artillery.
If neither side withdraws, begin another duel turn from step 1.

magic.rule: Certain spells and magic items can damage strongholds as listed.

entry.name: transmute_rock_to_mud
entry.rule: May transform earth beneath strongholds into mud to weaken foundations.
50% of the damage is recovered when the spell expires or is dispelled.

entry.name: move_earth
entry.rule: May shift ground beneath strongholds and cause earthquake-like structural damage.
Cannot be used if the stronghold is built on solid rock unless transmute rock to mud is used first.

overview.rule: A besieging army may dig one or more siege-mines.
Siege-mining excavates wooden-reinforced earthen tunnels under or around the stronghold, then burns supports to collapse tunnel and structure above.

construction_rules.rule: Each siege-mine is a construction project costing 1,000gp.
Each siege-mine must be supervised by an engineer.
No more than 100 workers may be assigned to each siege-mine.
When completed and ignited, a siege-mine deals 6d6x100 shp damage.
If a petard is used in the siege-mine, increase damage by 100 x the petard's damage.
Each siege-mine contains approximately 20,000 cubic feet of tunnel.
Construction rate is 20 cubic feet of tunnel per 1gp per day.
A besieger may pursue as many siege-mine projects as desired, limited by available engineers and workers.

risk_rules.rule: Workers assigned to siege-mining make a loyalty roll each week.
An unmodified loyalty roll of 2 causes a mining accident.
A mining accident destroys the mine, kills all assigned workers, and loses the value of the mine.
The supervising engineer may save versus Blast to escape death.

countermining.rule: Each day of a mining project, the defender may make a reconnaissance roll to detect the siege-mine.
Once detected, the defender may order one or more countermines.
Each countermine is a construction project supervised by an engineer.
Up to 100 workers may be assigned to each countermine.
Countermines require weekly loyalty rolls, with an unmodified 2 causing a mining accident.
Each countermine's construction rate is applied as a penalty to one siege-mine project's construction rate.

limits.limit: If a stronghold is built on solid rock, it cannot be reduced by siege-mining.
If a stronghold is entirely surrounded by water, or by a moat at least 10' deep, siege-mining is virtually impossible.

requirements.rule: Requires a successful Move Silently throw.

modifiers.rule: Modified by the opposing army leader's strategic ability.

results.rule: Success destroys 4d6 x 10 shp per class level.
Extra damage may be attempted by taking a -1 penalty per additional 4d6 x 10 shp.
Damage from arson is divided by 10 if the stronghold is stone.

requirements.rule: Requires a successful Hide in Shadows throw.

modifiers.rule: Modified by the opposing army leader's strategic ability.

results.rule: Success creates 1 breach in the stronghold.
Additional breaches may be created by taking a -1 penalty per additional breach.
Breaches created by subversion must be exploited immediately with an assault or are lost.

stronghold_repair.rule: After each day of reduction, the defending army may make repairs during the evening hours.
Wooden construction repairs at 5 shp per 1gp of construction rate.
Stone construction repairs at 1 shp per 1gp of construction rate.
Only half of all damage sustained during the siege can be repaired during the siege.
The remainder must be rebuilt after the siege at full construction cost.

overview.rule: If blockade and reduction fail to induce capitulation, the besieging army may assault.
Assault seeks capture through direct combat.
Assaults are decisive but costly.

resolving_assaults.turn_scale: Each assault turn represents approximately 10 minutes of hard fighting.

procedure.step: The besieging leader selects assaulting units.
Maximum assaulting units = 1 unit per point of unit capacity + 1 additional unit per breach.
The leader designates which units assault through breaches; all other assaulting units are assumed to use siege ladders.
Units not assigned to the assault remain in reserve and do not participate this turn.
The besieging leader selects any artillery or siege equipment used in the assault; these do not count against the maximum unit limit.
The defending leader selects defending units.
Maximum defending units = 1 unit per point of unit capacity.
Units not assigned to defense remain in reserve and do not participate this turn.
The defending leader selects any artillery or siege equipment used in defense; these do not count against the maximum unit limit.
Heroic PCs and NPCs may make heroic forays; all such forays are revealed and resolved simultaneously; lost units are then removed.
Each leader simultaneously rolls attack throws equal to the army's remaining battle rating.
Base target number is 16+, modified by assault attack throw modifiers.
Each successful attack throw scores 1 hit.
Each leader removes units from his army with combined battle rating equal to or greater than hits scored against his army.
Hits in excess of those needed to defeat all opposing units are ignored.
Apply hits simultaneously.
If all defending units are defeated and the defending army has no reserves, the stronghold is captured.
If all assaulting units are defeated and the besieging army has no reserves, the stronghold is liberated.
If neither end state occurs, the defending army may voluntarily surrender.
If the defender surrenders, the stronghold is captured.
If the defender does not surrender, the besieger may renew the assault or call it off.
If renewed, begin another assault turn from step 1.
If called off, the assault ends but the siege continues.
When the assault ends, determine casualties.

attack_throw_modifiers.rule: Assaulting unit attack throws suffer -2 unless the attacking unit is artillery, siege equipment, a flyer, or a unit assaulting through a breach.

battle_ratings_during_assaults.rule: Only the battle ratings of assaulting or defending units count toward army BR.
Reserve units do not count toward BR.
All defending infantry units gain +1 BR due to protection of the stronghold.
Assaulting cavalry not using a breach have BR reduced to one-quarter of base value, rounded up.

general_rules.rule: Artillery and siege equipment must be grouped into units to affect an assault.
Equipment not present in sufficient numbers to form a unit has no effect on the assault.
A leader is not required to risk artillery or siege equipment in an assault.
Artillery and siege equipment units have BR and function like ordinary assaulting or defending units unless a note states otherwise.
Artillery and siege equipment do not count against unit-capacity restrictions on assault or defense.
Maximum BR contributed by siege equipment is equal to the BR contributed by assaulting or defending troop units.

unit_size_rules.rule: Unit size is the minimum number of pieces required for effect.
For variable-size equipment such as rams, an oversized piece may qualify as a unit by itself if sufficiently large.

notes.entry: May make four attacks each assault turn, but breaks on an unmodified throw of 1; broken units are removed from the assault.
May only be deployed by the besieging army.
Provides a bonus attack throw on the first turn of an assault.
Absorbs one hit during an assault turn; absorbing a hit destroys the gallery or mantlet unit.
May make one attack throw each assault turn; a hit destroys a ram or screw unit.
Reduces the BR of the defending army by one.

acquisition.rule: If in supply, an army may acquire artillery and siege equipment from the market.
Either army may construct artillery and siege equipment as construction projects.

general_rules.rule: Use the same heroic foray mechanics as battles except as noted here.
Units of artillery and siege equipment may appear as foes for either side.

defending_the_stronghold.rule: Missile attacks targeting creatures defending the walls suffer a -4 penalty.
Creatures defending the walls gain +4 on saves versus Blast from artillery, burning oil, or similar effects.
On a successful save, creatures defending the walls take no damage even if the effect would normally deal half damage on a success.

encounter_distance.rule: Defending participants begin inside the stronghold.
Besieging participants begin outside the walls at a distance determined by stronghold site.
Roll encounter distance by site, then multiply by wall_height / 6'.

foe_selection.rule: When selecting foes, defending units are worth one additional point of BR.

unit_loss.rule: For each defeated unit, 50% of its troops rounded up are crippled or dead.
For each defeated unit, 50% of its troops rounded down are lightly wounded.

entry.rule: Besieging wounded recover during the next week.
Any surrendering troops also become prisoners.
Defending wounded recover during the next week.
Besieging wounded are left behind and become prisoners of the defenders.

post_battle_unit_management.rule: Half-strength units may be consolidated into fewer full-strength units.

prisoners.rule: Prisoners may be executed, kept as slaves, or ransomed.
Standard ransom or slave value is 40gp per prisoner.
Higher-level NPCs, monsters, and similar creatures may be worth more at Judge discretion.
Defenders usually cannot feed prisoners and will likely kill or ransom them.
Defenders may use prisoners as leverage during surrender negotiations.

general_end_conditions.entry: Defending army sallies forth and gives battle.
Besieging army captures or destroys the stronghold.

defending_army_sallies_forth.rule: If the defender exits the stronghold and gives battle, the siege ends and a pitched battle is fought immediately.
If the defender loses the pitched battle, it may retreat back into the stronghold or into an adjacent 6-mile hex, subject to pursuit either way.
If the defender wins the pitched battle, the besieger is subject to normal retreat and pursuit rules.

defending_army_surrenders.rule: Surrender may be voluntary or involuntary.
Voluntary surrender occurs through negotiation between leaders.
Involuntary surrender occurs when all units inside the stronghold fail loyalty rolls due to calamities.
Better surrender terms are more likely if the defender surrenders while some force remains intact.
Any surrender gives the besieging army victory.

besieging_army_departs_the_hex.rule: If the besieger leaves the hex with all units, the defender wins the siege.
The besieger may continue the siege by leaving at least one unit in the hex.

besieging_army_captures_the_stronghold.rule: The besieger wins if it captures the stronghold by assault.
The besieger wins if it destroys the stronghold by reduction.
If reduction destroys the stronghold, defending units must sally forth or surrender.

spoils_of_sieges.rule: Victorious siege spoils equal one month's wages of each defeated unit.
Each prisoner captured is worth 40gp if sold as a slave or ransomed.
Experience points are assigned as with a battle.
The stronghold and domain may also be pillaged for additional plunder.
Terms of voluntary surrender may forbid pillaging, but compliance depends on the victor.

overview.rule: Use the simplified system when only outcome and duration matter.
Cross-reference stronghold structural hit points with besieging army unit advantage on the duration table.
A numerical result is the number of days to capture the stronghold.
A result of 0 means the stronghold is captured without a fight.
A result of - means the besieger is not strong enough to capture the stronghold and can only attempt to starve out the defenders by blockade.

unit_advantage.rule: Unit advantage = besieging army units - defending army units.
Artillery and siege engines count as bonus units on both sides.

site_duration_modifiers.rule: Some stronghold sites multiply the duration indicated by the duration table.

casualties_in_simplified_sieges.rule: To assess casualties from a completed simplified siege, resolve a battle, not an assault, between besieging and defending armies.
This represents final collapse, sally, or cleanup after reduction.
Defending units that suffer Flee are treated as cowering in the rubble rather than increasing distance from attackers.
Defending units that suffer Rout are treated as having surrendered to the besieger.

off_camera_and_intervention_guidance.rule: The simplified table is useful for off-camera sieges.
If PCs intervene during an ongoing simplified siege, calculate current wall condition and supplies by elapsed time.
When the listed duration has fully elapsed, the stronghold has 0 shp.
When half the listed duration has elapsed, the stronghold has 50% of its shp remaining.
Apply the same proportional logic for other elapsed fractions.
